subject: Path loadings and effective sample size calculations

messages.author: c78bfd9857351762
messages.subject: Path loadings and effective sample size calculations
parts:
Just a couple of questions to clarify the GWAS by subtraction method:

1.  Would I use the estimates from the SEM without SNPs model as path loadings for the GWAS by subtraction model?
2.  Would I also use these estimates to calculate effective sample size of the GWAS by subtraction (adjusting estimates estj by multiplying by residual heterogeneity, p 6 Supp Info, your paper)?
3.  Where I may need sample size (total cases and total controls) for downstream analyses, would I use effective sample size, the sample size of the larger GWAS (EA), or maybe the sample size of smaller GWAS (CP) used to generate GWAS by subtraction?

Thanks in advance! 

Dan

messages.author: ac421cf36d1a4c37
messages.subject: Re: Path loadings and effective sample size calculations
parts:
Hi Dan,

1. You can estimate the model without SNPs, yes. But you don't need to save the estimate and fix it to that value in the model with the SNP. It is estimated in that model as well.

2. Yes, the lambda used for the equation on pp. 6-7 can come from the no SNP model.

3. I think this depends on what you are using N or effective N for. If you are estimating the SNP h2 of NonCog by entering the NonCog sumstats into LDSC, then in order for it to be on the scale of EA variance (i.e. the proportion of variance in EA that ia attributable to NonCog genetics) then it would probably be sensible to use the N for EA (of course, you already get this quantity from the no-SNP model, so estimating LDSC again with the new sumstats is a bit redundant). For other applications, it may be more desirable to use effective N as calculated using the Mallard method referenced in our supp. Also please note that you say that you may need sample size in terms of total cases and controls, but our application in Demange uses quantitative phenotypes. For a further discussion of effective N for case/control GWAS, you can check out the chain from earlier this week initiated by Lucy (https://groups.google.com/g/genomic-sem-users/c/VTBe0vLqmnU/m/DGODqH-VBQAJ).

I hope that's helpful,

All the best,

Elliot
